protocol.purpose: Fresh development verification plus read-only shadow collision/loss instrumentation; no terminal or optimizer execution
protocol.schedule: For each case: AD base; epsilon 1 four blocks; AD base; epsilon 2 four blocks; AD base. Each block begins with a base forward evaluation; signs alternate (+,-),(-,+),(+,-),(-,+). Fixed case order.
protocol.observer_scope: Independent shadow kernels before original grid_op/g2p. Recompute inputs and tangential norm, do not divide or write simulator fields. Original forward/backward kernels unmodified. Shadow arithmetic can differ from compiled temporaries. Store per-substep contact masks and per-action MILK L1 sign snapshots.

gate.requires: All five cases pass both predeclared epsilons; observer runs have no zero/<=EPS/invalid shadow norms, meet baseline loss/AD agreement, and fresh-process control meets agreement. Empirical ranges are descriptive, not confidence bounds. No noise allowance is added to the AD/FD tolerance.

protocol.scope: Four/eight-step partial diff loss with original max_loss_steps=1000; no original terminal step 999. Passing is engineering readiness only, not contact/physics correctness or paper replication. No automatic transition to terminal/optimization. Prior experiment files and failed gate remain unchanged.

instrumentation_amendment.reason: Original observer indexed records by local f; upstream max_substeps_local=20 reuses slots. Original counters aggregate multiple times and original masks retain only last visits. They cannot validate per-global-substep identity changes.
instrumentation_amendment.correction: Use cur_substep_global as recording index while retaining local f for all simulator reads. Native source, derivative criteria and original artifacts unchanged.
instrumentation_amendment.scope: Rerun only two observer/reference blocks in a new process, 18 forward evaluations / 8 reverse passes. Supplement existing numerical verification and fresh controls; not a numerical retry-until-pass.
instrumentation_amendment.original_mask_analysis_failure: Mask/counter mismatch; e.g. particle counters 81208 versus 40604 identities in a local frame, unused later global frames.

original_observer_invalid.reason: Local-memory index reused every 20 substeps. Per-global-substep masks overwritten while counters accumulated.
original_observer_invalid.action: Retain original raw artifacts; exclude original masks from gate and branch-identity claims. Rerun corrected recording under instrumentation-amendment.json.

observer_positive_controls.scope: Synthetic fixture exercises actual observer function, not native collision physics or simulation trajectories.

findings: The native terminal helper selects a WATER particle with NumPy argmin, derives ranks with argsort, writes its position as best_particle_pos, and sets a height-count attraction scale. These assignments are outside Taichi autodiff.

best_particle_pos, attraction_score and attraction_scale are allocated without needs_grad. Native backward kernels differentiate particle coordinates holding those assigned fields fixed; this is a surrogate derivative.

Finite differences that rerun target selection can change the selected position, ranking/membership and height-count scale. They test a different functional dependency from simply holding those fields constant. A mismatch must not automatically be labelled simulator-gradient failure.
The native backward terminal path invokes the selection helper again. Any frozen-target diagnostic must preserve the same explicit target on forward and backward, rather than only freezing forward.
No terminal term was evaluated in this experiment. The original step-999 objective and full horizon remain unverified.
proposed_next_test: Save a separate protocol for an explicitly shortened terminal diagnostic after assessing the development gate.
Record chosen target identity/position, selected-membership hash and scale for base and perturbed runs.
Compare recomputed-target and explicitly frozen-target modes as separate objectives. Preserve native backward semantics and make any diagnostic target override explicit.
Measure loss precision/noise and validate each mode against suitable differences before optimizer or long-horizon claims.

def find_best_particle(self, s, f):
        x = self.sim.get_x()
        used = self.sim.get_used()
        mat = self.particle_mat.to_numpy()
        loss = np.abs(x[:, 1] - 0.05)
        loss[np.logical_not(used)] = 1000
        loss[mat != WATER] = 1000
        best_particle_id = np.argmin(loss)
        self.best_particle_pos.from_numpy(x[best_particle_id])

        dist = np.linalg.norm(x - x[best_particle_id], axis=1)
        dist[np.logical_not(used)] = 1000
        dist[mat != WATER] = 1000
        score = np.argsort(np.argsort(dist))
        self.attraction_score.from_numpy(score)

        x[mat != WATER] = np.array([-100, -100, -100])
        x[np.logical_not(used)] = np.array([-100, -100, -100])
        self.attraction_scale[None] = np.sum(x[:, 1] > 0.55) / 12500

conclusions: All five cases pass both new epsilon checks under a frozen engineering gate; strict AD/FD tolerance 5% plus absolute .01, no extra noise allowance. Largest median discrepancy about 1.78%; this is not scientific derivative-accuracy validation.

The earlier-action eight-step residual remains about .45-.47% at the smaller fresh scales, beyond observed repeat ranges. Fresh-process median AD differs by only .583 (~.00356%) from same-process, so this control does not explain the residual.

Corrected shadow observations find no zero, <=EPS or invalid/huge tangential norms in the six observed base/plus/minus runs. Min observed grid norm is about5.19e-7. No particle contact is active in these short shadow runs. This does not establish absence under other conditions or exact native intermediate values.

Original observer local-memory index bug was caught by mask/counter verification. Original files retained, numerical protocol/results unchanged; only recording uses global index in a separately declared rerun. Corrected 12 NPZ artifacts validate and synthetic positive controls detect zero norm and global-slot separation.
Fresh and corrected-observer baseline controls meet their predeclared tolerances; exported resets match, without proving equality of every hidden state/buffer.

177 forward evaluations and34 reverse passes across original main,fresh,corrected workers; no terminal test, optimizer, SI calibration, physics validation, paper reproduction or RDF approval. Old failed gate remains unchanged.
